analysis.investment_thesis: Aurionpro is a genuine BFSI technology turnaround — revenue tripled from ₹374 Cr (FY21) to ₹1,173 Cr (FY25) with ROCE expanding to 18% and debt nearly eliminated. However, acquisition-fueled growth (investing outflows of ₹421 Cr in FY25 alone), a complex multi-product sprawl, and dangerously low promoter conviction at 26.9% make this a story to watch rather than own at conviction size.
key_strengths: Rapid recent acceleration: revenue CAGR ~33% over FY21-25, operating profit ₹84 Cr → ₹242 Cr with expanding margins
Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E: 0.02, borrowings collapsed from ₹154 Cr to ₹30 Cr) with ₹269 Cr cash
ROCE at 18.1% clears Munger's 15% threshold; finance costs fell 12.4% CAGR over 9 years showing capital discipline improving
key_risks: Acquisition binge: investing CF was -₹203 Cr (FY24) then -₹421 Cr (FY25) — serial acquirers rarely compound well without a strong integration playbook
Low promoter stake of 26.88% signals limited skin-in-the-game; management's alignment with long-term shareholders is unclear
FCF of only ₹62 Cr vs net profit ₹188 Cr in FY25 (FCF conversion ~33%) — heavy capex and working capital absorption raises earnings quality concerns
red_flags: FY21 net loss of -₹192 Cr (vs EBITDA of ₹223 Cr) implies massive write-offs — likely from prior bad acquisitions, a pattern that may recur given current M&A pace
9-year revenue CAGR of only 5.7% reveals that the business destroyed value for nearly a decade before the recent revival
Fragmented product portfolio spanning transaction banking, trade finance, smart cities, data centers, and AI labs — complexity is the enemy of durable returns
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying inversion first: Aurionpro nearly destroyed itself between FY16-FY21, with revenue collapsing from ₹710 Cr to ₹374 Cr and booking a ₹192 Cr net loss in FY21. The culprit appears to be prior acquisitions and write-downs (other income swung -₹118 Cr in FY21). Now the company is repeating the acquisition playbook at pace — ₹624 Cr in investing outflows over just two years. The critical question Munger would ask: does management have a proven integration capability, or is it simply buying revenue growth? The evidence is ambiguous at best. The 26.88% promoter stake is a structural concern — insiders own barely a quarter of the business they run.

On the positive side, the recent operational quality is genuine. Operating margins expanded to 17.4%, EBITDA nearly doubled in three years, and the balance sheet is clean. Forward P/E of ~17x is not outrageous if 25-30% earnings growth sustains. But ROIC is not yet the 20%+ that signals a true compounding machine, FCF conversion is weak (₹62 Cr FCF vs ₹188 Cr net profit), and the business complexity across 8+ product lines makes it hard to identify a durable, defensible moat. This is a business recovering from past sins and currently riding BFSI digitization tailwinds — worth monitoring, but not a Munger-grade fortress at this stage.
